_meta.googleAntigravityStaging: google-antigravity staging: the Antigravity Go harness owns the conversation history and never sends role:"tool" messages. Measured on the native Gemini path (2026-10-05): the follow-up request after get_weather arrives as [user, assistant{tool_calls:[get_weather]}, assistant ""] -- no tool message, and the tool-call id is aimock's synthetic one, not the fixture's. hasToolResult/toolCallId therefore never fire here, so every leg is staged on turnIndex (aimock's count of assistant messages; the real flow adds 2 per tool round-trip). Deployed aimock (staging/prod) runs --proxy-only, which forces the STRICT turnIndex gate: a fixture whose turnIndex is not exactly the assistant count is rejected, and an untagged fixture matches at every position. Local stacks run without a proxy and use the relaxed rule (highest turnIndex <= assistant count wins). Every leg here is positioned so both rules give the same answer.

fixtures._comment: tool-rendering-default-catchall — leg 1: emit get_weather(Tokyo). `turnIndex: 0` pins the POSITION. The previous leg was untagged: under the strict gate deployed aimock uses, an untagged leg matches at EVERY position, so after each tool round-trip it re-emitted get_weather forever (the PNI-570/PNI-571 loop: thousands of cycles per staging stream). `toolName` keeps the leg out of requests from agents that do not declare get_weather. Registered BEFORE the turnIndex-0 fallback so it wins the tie whenever get_weather is declared. The built-in default renderer renders [data-testid='copilot-tool-render'][data-tool-name='get_weather'] with a status pill [data-testid='copilot-tool-render-status'].

tool-rendering-default-catchall — leg 2: narration after the get_weather result, at the measured follow-up position (assistant count 2). Replaces a toolCallId-gated follow-up that could never match (see _meta.googleAntigravityStaging).

response.content: Tokyo is 22°C and partly cloudy — the default catchall renderer displayed the tool card above.

fixtures._comment: tool-rendering-default-catchall — leg 2 at assistant count 1, for a follow-up that carries only the tool-call turn. Without it the relaxed rule (local) falls back to leg 1 and calls get_weather again, and the strict rule (deployed) finds no match.

response.content: Tokyo is 22°C and partly cloudy — the default catchall renderer displayed the tool card above.

fixtures._comment: tool-rendering-default-catchall — fallback for an agent that does not declare get_weather: narrated content, no tool call. Registered AFTER leg 1 so leg 1 wins the turnIndex-0 tie whenever get_weather IS declared.

response.content: The weather in Tokyo is currently 22°C with partly cloudy skies and light easterly winds.
